title: fix(host-kit): pin ps lstart reads to the C locale so daemon stop finds a live daemon

files.patch:
@@ -119,7 +119,9 @@ test('a record whose process is gone or was replaced is not a running daemon', (
     processStartTime:
       process.platform === 'linux'
         ? 'linux:00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000:0'
-        : 'Thu Jan  1 00:00:00 1970',
+        : process.platform === 'win32'
+          ? '000000000000000000000'
+          : 'posix:1000',
     plugins: [ACTIVE],
   });
   expect(readDaemonStatus(resolveDaemonPaths(stateDir)).state).toBe('stopped');

   mkdtempForTestSync,

 pinOwnProcessStartTime(hostProcess);
@@ -467,7 +468,9 @@ test('keeps corrupt claims visible and requires --stale for uncertain reclaimabl

         ownerPid: owner.pid,
-        ownerStartTime: 'different-readable-start-time',

@@ -420,6 +420,7 @@ Runner and daemon lifecycle (applies to simulators too):
   On iOS simulators, open prepares app accessibility before launching an app or URL. If a running app has an empty accessibility tree after an earlier XCTest session, use open <app> --relaunch, then snapshot -i. A preparation failure is logged and does not block launch.
   A command that needs the shared local daemon starts it for its state dir when none runs (device status and device release --stale never contact one). When the running daemon comes from another version or build, the command replaces it only if the daemon reports no work: no in-flight request, session, repair session, or live lease (a streaming resumable upload and a host human-control hold that names no lease are not counted); otherwise it fails with details.reason daemon-busy and leaves the daemon alone. A daemon that agreed to leave is waited for up to 60 s and never signaled while it drains; one still running then fails with details.reason daemon-drain-timeout unless it answers nothing and is provably a daemon process, which is force-retired. A daemon from a release that predates this check is never replaced and fails with daemon-incompatible. End a busy or older daemon deliberately with agent-device daemon stop --state-dir <path>. Node clients pick daemonLifecycle 'attach' (never starts or replaces a daemon; fails with daemon-not-running or daemon-incompatible) or 'managed' (the default until 0.22), and ensureDaemon() starts or replaces one explicitly.
   daemon stop --state-dir <path> stops a detached daemon with process signals after verifying its identity, and waits up to 75 s for the daemon to finish its own teardown before it forces the exit. For a live embedded runtime, stop refuses with details.reason daemon-owner-embedded and a hint naming the host PID. Close that runtime in its host process with the handle returned by startAgentDevice(). Stop refuses live unrecognized ownership with daemon-owner-unrecognized and sends no request or signal. Stop retires an embedded or unrecognized registration when its recorded host lifetime has provably exited. Without --clean, an unreadable daemon.json fails with daemon-record-unreadable. daemon status shows host-owned or owner-not-recognized. Managed clients reuse a matching embedded runtime. Takeover, drain, and timeout recovery refuse a live embedded or unrecognized owner without a signal; a provably exited owner is retired so the state directory stays usable. Detached stop and cleanup use the lifetime and ownership from one registration read. --clean requires proven detached ownership; embedded, unrecognized and unreadable records fail with daemon-clean-not-detached because that cleanup walks the owner's whole process tree.
+  A macOS or BSD daemon registered before this release stores a raw lstart rendering, which cannot be compared against this build's start-time token: stop then refuses with details.terminationReason identity-unverified and sends no signal, keeping daemon.json and the lock. Older registrations that store a Linux /proc or Windows start-time token still stop normally; a Linux registration read through the ps fallback (for example with an unreadable boot_id) has the macOS and BSD limits. Stop such a daemon with the same (older) agent-device build that started it, or end it as its owner (SIGTERM to the recorded PID) before running this build against that state dir; deleting the state dir also works once the owner is known dead. On macOS or BSD, do not run an older and a newer build on one host: runner leases and device claims are host-global, so the older build can read a newer start-time token as a reused process, and records that an older build wrote stay unverified until their owner stops the process. That covers the daemon registration, the companion tunnel, runner leases, and other records that store a process start time.
   On a machine shared by several agents, set AGENT_DEVICE_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS to also expire an individual session that has taken a host-global device claim and then received no commands for that long; the claim is released and the next command on that session answers SESSION_NOT_FOUND with details.reason SESSION_IDLE_EXPIRED naming the window and the device. Off by default, because on a shared host "idle" and "thinking" are indistinguishable: only set it where an abandoned claim blocking every other agent is the worse failure. Sessions holding a remote lease or any active capture (recording, logs, audio, performance, or trace) are never expired this way.
   A stale iOS runner lease — its owner process dead, or its AGENT_DEVICE_STATE_DIR deleted — is reclaimed automatically instead of failing with "is already owned by another agent-device daemon". A live owner's runner is also reclaimed when the requesting daemon holds the host-global device claim for that device: claims are exclusive, so holding one proves the runner's owner released the device and merely kept the runner warm. The error remains only for owners outside claim arbitration (a pre-claims build, or daemons pointed at different claim stores).

@@ -93,7 +93,7 @@ Device claims and the daemon:
 - `device release --stale` settles the durable resources of an owner that provably can't release its claim (its process exited or a newer daemon replaced it), then clears the claim. Live, uncertain, PID-reused, corrupt, and deleted-state-directory claims are refused with the reason. See [Sessions](/docs/sessions#release-a-device-another-session-or-workspace-holds).
 - A claim conflict on `open` fails with `DEVICE_IN_USE` and names the conflict in `error.details.reason`: `DEVICE_CLAIM_LIVE_OWNER` (a live owner holds the device), `DEVICE_CLAIM_RECOVERY_PENDING` (a dead or superseded owner's durable resources are still being settled), or `DEVICE_CLAIM_OWNER_UNCERTAIN` (the owner's liveness could not be proven). Each is a pre-dispatch refusal: nothing reached the device.
 - A command that needs the shared local daemon starts it for its state directory when none runs; `device status` and `device release --stale` never contact one. When the running daemon comes from another version or build, the command replaces it only if it reports no work: no request in flight, no session, no repair session and no live lease. A resumable upload still streaming and a host human-control hold that names no lease are not counted, so a replacement can end them. Otherwise the command fails with `daemon-busy` and leaves the daemon alone. A daemon from a release that predates this check is never replaced, and fails with `daemon-incompatible`. End a busy or older daemon deliberately with `daemon stop`. Node.js clients choose this per client; see [Daemon lifecycle](/docs/client-api#daemon-lifecycle).
-- `daemon stop --state-dir <path>` stops a detached local daemon with process signals after verifying its identity. It waits up to 75 seconds for the daemon to finish its own teardown before it forces the exit. `--clean` also removes the Apple runner processes and leases that daemon retained.
+- `daemon stop --state-dir <path>` stops a detached local daemon with process signals after verifying its identity. It waits up to 75 seconds for the daemon to finish its own teardown before it forces the exit. `--clean` also removes the Apple runner processes and leases that daemon retained. A macOS or BSD daemon registered before this release stores a raw `lstart` rendering, which this build's start-time token cannot be compared against: stop then refuses with `details.terminationReason: identity-unverified`, sends no signal, and keeps `daemon.json` and the lock. Older registrations that store a Linux `/proc` or Windows start-time token still stop normally; a Linux registration read through the `ps` fallback (for example with an unreadable `boot_id`) has the macOS and BSD limits. Stop such a daemon with the same older build that started it, or end it as its owner (`SIGTERM` to the recorded PID) before using this build against that state dir; removing the state dir is safe once the owner is known dead. On macOS or BSD, do not run an older and a newer build on one host: runner leases and device claims are host-global, so the older build can read a newer start-time token as a reused process, and records that an older build wrote stay unverified until their owner stops the process. That covers the daemon registration, the companion tunnel, runner leases, and other records that store a process start time.
 - `daemon stop` refuses a live embedded runtime with `details.reason: daemon-owner-embedded` and a hint naming the host PID. Close it in its host process with the handle returned by `startAgentDevice()`. Stop refuses live unrecognized ownership with `daemon-owner-unrecognized`. Neither refusal sends a request or signal. Stop retires an embedded or unrecognized registration when its recorded host lifetime has provably exited. Without `--clean`, an unreadable `daemon.json` fails with `daemon-record-unreadable`. `--clean` requires proven detached ownership; embedded, unrecognized and unreadable records fail with `daemon-clean-not-detached`. `daemon status` shows `host-owned` or `owner-not-recognized`. See [Daemon lifecycle](/docs/client-api#daemon-lifecycle).
 - `daemon status [--state-dir <path>] [--json]` reads the daemon's record without contacting it. For a running daemon it lists every provider it registered, built in or installed, and the reason any plugin failed to register. See [provider plugins](/docs/plugins).
 - A `--state-dir` or `AGENT_DEVICE_STATE_DIR` you pass to these commands must be a private directory of your own account, because the daemon's record, lock, log, and recordings live in it. agent-device checks it before it reads anything and refuses one another account owns or can write, with the step that ends the refusal in the error. See [Supported environment variables](/docs/configuration#supported-environment-variables).
